subject.title: Cron job `delivered: false` when deliveryBestEffort: true and interim-message guard fires without active subagents

question: Should best-effort delivery bypass the stale-interim suppression policy after completed descendant activity, or should that policy remain and only incorrect descendant attribution be fixed?
rationale: The prior merged fix intentionally narrowed only active-descendant waiting and suppression; extending it to stale interim text changes the established delivery policy rather than mechanically repairing the proven active-subagent bug.

options.title: Keep stale-interim protection
options.body: Retain suppression for genuine completed descendants and investigate only a concrete false registry association from a captured run trace.

options.title: Redefine best-effort delivery
options.body: Make best-effort always deliver non-silent parent text, accepting possible provisional acknowledgments after genuine descendant activity.

recommendation.title: Keep stale-interim protection
recommendation.body: Retain suppression for genuine completed descendants and investigate only a concrete false registry association from a captured run trace.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent central cron delivery history and the related merged-fix discussion make this the strongest available routing candidate.
